# They all output candidate distributions. Why do their readout and caching boundaries differ?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/system-one/typed-readout.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 9 topic entries / 4 representative comparisons

Typed decisions constrain the output space, but avoiding long generated sentences does not prescribe a single architecture. LLM2Jev reads the language probability of option labels; System One reranking reads candidate letters at the first answer position; MJev-Spatial reuses native attention Q/K; and MetaEncoder encodes requests and candidates separately. Trace scoring dependencies before judging what can be cached, whether open retrieval is possible, or how continuous outputs are discretized.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Separate a single readout from a single task step

LLM2Jev and System One reranking both read probabilities directly, but an option label can span multiple tokens, and reranking must verify that each letter is a single token. A single MJev-Spatial candidate readout does not make the whole spatial task a single call: point localization chooses three successive 3×3 regions and counting uses a hierarchical representation. Compare the total forward passes and inputs for the same task, not just the final output format.

Sources: [LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them](../../../../foundation-models/2610.02076-llm2jev/README-en.md) · [Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en.md) · [MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22276-mjev-spatial/README-en.md)

### Caching gains come from dependencies

MetaEncoder encodes each candidate from its own content, which supports building an offline vector index. System One reranking places candidates in a shared context, so changing the other candidates may change the contextualized representation. A closed-set MetaEncoder request may still contain its options: reusable candidate caches do not imply that the request vector is option-invariant. One favors indexability, the other joint comparison; neither interface guarantees higher accuracy.

Sources: [MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface](../../../../foundation-models/2610.11316-metaencoder/README-en.md) · [Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Both output candidate probabilities. Why can MetaEncoder pre-encode candidates while System One reranking generally cannot? {#cross-candidate-cache-dependency}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** MetaEncoder runs its candidate encoder independently, without reading the current request or other candidates. In joint reranking, candidates are contextualized in the same prompt; caching a representation outside that set does not guarantee the same score. Computation is cacheable when its dependencies are unchanged, regardless of whether the output is a probability.

    **Illustrative example:** One tool description can be encoded once for retrieval by a thousand dual-encoder queries. A VLM comparing it jointly against five other tools receives a different input when those five competitors change.

    Sources: [MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface](../../../../foundation-models/2610.11316-metaencoder/README-en.md) · [Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en.md)

### How can counting and point localization be cast as choices, and why is this not the same as a single ordinary multiple-choice question? {#cross-spatial-choice-granularity}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** MJev-Spatial decomposes numeric outputs into bounded discrete decisions, refining regions over multiple point-localization steps. LLM2Jev instead assigns a distribution to fixed given options. In spatial refinement the next input depends on the region chosen before it, and errors can propagate across stages. Account for the full pipeline rather than each softmax in isolation.

    **Illustrative example:** First choose the upper-right region of a 3×3 grid, then subdivide that region of the original image. A perfectly precise second choice cannot recover a location excluded by the first.

    Sources: [MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22276-mjev-spatial/README-en.md) · [LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them](../../../../foundation-models/2610.02076-llm2jev/README-en.md)

### If the top candidate gets a normalized probability of 0.9, is the model 90% confident that it is correct? {#cross-conditional-mass-confidence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not necessarily. System One reranking normalizes only over candidate letters even when their total vocabulary mass is tiny. MetaEncoder's temperature-scaled softmax likewise expresses relative fit among the current candidates. Calibration against the actual correctness rate requires separately labeled data; a relative share alone is not a correctness guarantee.

    **Illustrative example:** If two candidate letters have vocabulary probabilities of 0.009 and 0.001, candidate-only normalization gives 0.9 and 0.1 even though the remaining 0.99 mass falls on other tokens.

    Sources: [Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en.md) · [MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface](../../../../foundation-models/2610.11316-metaencoder/README-en.md)
